cap: In the male pelvis the ductus deferens crosses over the ureter, widens into an ampulla and joins the seminal vesicle to form the ejaculatory duct, which opens on the seminal colliculus of the prostatic urethra. Peritoneum dips only to the rectovesical pouch; Denonvilliers fascia lies between the prostate and rectum, so a digital rectal exam feels the posterior prostate. During emission the internal urethral sphincter closes; if it fails, semen flows back into the bladder.
teach: Read the figure in three steps. First, follow the sperm: the ductus deferens loops over the ureter, widens into an ampulla and joins the seminal vesicle duct to form the ejaculatory duct, which pierces the prostate and opens on the seminal colliculus. Second, find the bladder neck: the internal urethral sphincter there is smooth muscle that sympathetic alpha-1 receptors close during emission, while the external sphincter is skeletal muscle around the membranous urethra. Third, look behind: the rectovesical pouch is the lowest peritoneal recess in men, Denonvilliers fascia separates the rectum from the prostate and seminal vesicles, and a finger in the rectum feels the posterior prostate.
